# DEEP OROPHARYNGEAL INFECTIONS

Deep oropharyngeal infections may threaten life and must be treated immediately. Assess the risk of airway compromise and monitor the airway if it is threatened. These infections are more common in people with diabetes mellitus and are caused by mixed organisms including streptococcus sp., Staphylococcus aureus and anaerobes. Perform CT scan to diagnose abscess. ENT and Infectious Diseases consults are essential.

## Duration of therapy

If the patient's condition worsens or does not improve during the first 48 hours of antimicrobial therapy, surgical drainage is indicated. If surgical drainage is done, antimicrobials are usually continued for 48 hours after the procedure. If surgical drainage is not done, 2 weeks of antimicrobial therapy until clinical improvement is observed (e.g. resolution of fever and leukocytosis) is appropriate.

---

References:

- Hull et al, Current Infectious Disease Reports. 2005, 7(1)17-27
- Mandell chapter: Infections of the Oral Cavity, Neck, and Head
- Ogle, Dent Clin N Am. 2017, 61(2)235-252
- Reynolds et al. Lung. 2009, 187(5)271-279
- Sanford keyword: Tooth, Odontogenic Infection, Ludwig's Angina
- Up-to-Date article: Submandibular space infections (Ludwig's angina)
Therapy:
Preferred:
Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h for 7 days ($) [R]

Alternative: [Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h ($) [DI]

## Risk factors for MRSA or gram-positive cocci in clusters on gram stain, in addition to one of the above antimicrobial regimens

< ADD > vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12 hours ($) [R]

## Immunocompromised patient or severe infection

Immunocompromised patients require additional coverage for Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

Preferred:
< AND > vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Cefepime 2 gm IV q12h ($$) [R] < AND > vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q 12 hours ($) [R] for 7 days

## Step-down treatment after initial intravenous therapy. Adjust duration based on criteria above.

Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h for 7 days ($) [R]

*Local guidance (Omaha CDSS, Inpatient):*
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q8h extended infusion ($$) [R]
